Recommended Improvements After Baseline Add a small evals folder with question, expected answer, expected source, and answer_should_exist fields. Add a retrieval-only test that calls /retrieve and checks whether expected sources appear in the top five results. Add reranking if the vector retriever returns plausible but weak context. Add hybrid keyword and vector search if exact IDs, codes, or named clauses are often missed. Add stronger PDF parsing or OCR only if the target documents require it.

Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

Non-Functional Requirements NFR-001: The demo must run on a low-cost EC2 instance for portfolio evaluation, with the understanding that indexing may be slower on very small machines. NFR-002: The browser interface should remain simple enough for a non-technical evaluator to upload documents and ask questions without setup instructions inside the app. NFR-003: The backend should expose explicit health checks so deployment problems can be diagnosed through curl before testing the UI. NFR-004: The repository should be small, clean, and free of generated local artifacts. NFR-005: The application should make retrieval evidence visible to reduce hallucination risk and improve trust. Known Scope Boundaries The current release does not include authentication. Public demo deployments should only be used temporarily or behind a controlled network. The current release does not include reranking. Retrieval uses vector similarity and a small top-k value suitable for a lightweight demo. The current release does not include hybrid BM25 plus vector search. Exact identifier queries may be improved in a future version. The current release does not process scanned PDFs with OCR. Text must be extractable from the uploaded files. The current release does not store collections in S3 or a managed vector database. Local disk is used for simplicity and cost control. Acceptance Criteria A reviewer can upload the full demo corpus and ask: What is FR-006? The answer should mention the retrieval-only endpoint and cite this product requirements document. A reviewer can ask whether authentication is included. The answer should state that authentication is not included in the current release. A reviewer can ask what success target is defined for fact-seeking questions. The answer should report the 85 percent target. A reviewer can ask whether scanned PDFs are supported. The answer should say OCR is not included and text must be extractable.

Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

For numeric spreadsheet questions, the system should report exact values from the workbook and avoid rounding unless asked. Failure Modes to Watch The retriever may return a semantically similar but wrong document when multiple files discuss the same feature. The model may cite a filename even when the retrieved snippet does not support the statement. Spreadsheet rows may be missed if a sheet is too large and relevant rows are split away from headers. The answer model may over-answer when the user asks about information that is absent from the corpus. Very broad questions may retrieve generic overview chunks instead of the most specific operational details. Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health. If the backend direct health check works but the Nginx-routed health check returns 404, the Nginx site is probably not linked, the default site is still enabled, or Nginx was not reloaded. If SSH times out, check the instance state, public IPv4 address, route table, network ACL, and security group source IP. If SSH reports bad key permissions on Windows, move the PEM file to the .ssh folder and restrict file access to the current Windows user. Operational Commands View API logs with sudo journalctl -u insight-api -f. View UI logs with sudo journalctl -u insight-ui -f. Validate Nginx config with sudo nginx -t before reloading Nginx. Update the deployed application with cd /opt/insight-ai/app followed by bash deploy/update_app.sh. Stop the instance when not demonstrating the project to reduce cost. Runbook-Specific Facts The canonical EC2 storage path for this demo is /opt/insight-ai/data. The canonical public web port is 80, not 8501. The canonical backend port is 8000, but it should only bind to localhost. The canonical UI port is 8501, but it should only bind to localhost. The intended service names are insight-api and insight-ui.

Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

Non-Functional Requirements NFR-001: The demo must run on a low-cost EC2 instance for portfolio evaluation, with the understanding that indexing may be slower on very small machines. NFR-002: The browser interface should remain simple enough for a non-technical evaluator to upload documents and ask questions without setup instructions inside the app. NFR-003: The backend should expose explicit health checks so deployment problems can be diagnosed through curl before testing the UI. NFR-004: The repository should be small, clean, and free of generated local artifacts. NFR-005: The application should make retrieval evidence visible to reduce hallucination risk and improve trust. Known Scope Boundaries The current release does not include authentication. Public demo deployments should only be used temporarily or behind a controlled network. The current release does not include reranking. Retrieval uses vector similarity and a small top-k value suitable for a lightweight demo. The current release does not include hybrid BM25 plus vector search. Exact identifier queries may be improved in a future version. The current release does not process scanned PDFs with OCR. Text must be extractable from the uploaded files. The current release does not store collections in S3 or a managed vector database. Local disk is used for simplicity and cost control. Acceptance Criteria A reviewer can upload the full demo corpus and ask: What is FR-006? The answer should mention the retrieval-only endpoint and cite this product requirements document. A reviewer can ask whether authentication is included. The answer should state that authentication is not included in the current release. A reviewer can ask what success target is defined for fact-seeking questions. The answer should report the 85 percent target. A reviewer can ask whether scanned PDFs are supported. The answer should say OCR is not included and text must be extractable.

Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health. If the backend direct health check works but the Nginx-routed health check returns 404, the Nginx site is probably not linked, the default site is still enabled, or Nginx was not reloaded. If SSH times out, check the instance state, public IPv4 address, route table, network ACL, and security group source IP. If SSH reports bad key permissions on Windows, move the PEM file to the .ssh folder and restrict file access to the current Windows user. Operational Commands View API logs with sudo journalctl -u insight-api -f. View UI logs with sudo journalctl -u insight-ui -f. Validate Nginx config with sudo nginx -t before reloading Nginx. Update the deployed application with cd /opt/insight-ai/app followed by bash deploy/update_app.sh. Stop the instance when not demonstrating the project to reduce cost. Runbook-Specific Facts The canonical EC2 storage path for this demo is /opt/insight-ai/data. The canonical public web port is 80, not 8501. The canonical backend port is 8000, but it should only bind to localhost. The canonical UI port is 8501, but it should only bind to localhost. The intended service names are insight-api and insight-ui.

For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time. For numeric spreadsheet questions, the system should report exact values from the workbook and avoid rounding unless asked. Failure Modes to Watch The retriever may return a semantically similar but wrong document when multiple files discuss the same feature. The model may cite a filename even when the retrieved snippet does not support the statement. Spreadsheet rows may be missed if a sheet is too large and relevant rows are split away from headers. The answer model may over-answer when the user asks about information that is absent from the corpus. Very broad questions may retrieve generic overview chunks instead of the most specific operational details. Recommended Improvements After Baseline Add a small evals folder with question, expected answer, expected source, and answer_should_exist fields. Add a retrieval-only test that calls /retrieve and checks whether expected sources appear in the top five results. Add reranking if the vector retriever returns plausible but weak context. Add hybrid keyword and vector search if exact IDs, codes, or named clauses are often missed. Add stronger PDF parsing or OCR only if the target documents require it.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Non-Functional Requirements NFR-001: The demo must run on a low-cost EC2 instance for portfolio evaluatio...

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. sources.text: Non-Functional Requirements NFR-001: The demo must run on a low-cost EC2 instance for portfolio evaluation, with the understanding that indexing may be slower on very small machines. NFR-002: The browser interface should remain simple enough for a non-technical evaluator to upload documents and ask questions without setup instructions inside the app. NFR-003: The backend should expose explicit health checks so deployment problems can be diagnosed through curl before testing the UI. NFR-004: The repository should be small, clean, and free of generated local artifacts. NFR-005: The application should make retrieval evidence visible to reduce hallucination risk and improve trust. Known Scope Boundaries The current release does not include authentication. Public demo deployments should only be used temporarily or behind a controlled network. The current release does not include reranking. Retrieval uses vector similarity and a small top-k value suitable for a lightweight demo. The current release does not include hybrid BM25 plus vector search. Exact identifier queries may be improved in a future version. The current release does not process scanned PDFs with OCR. Text must be extractable from the uploaded files. The current release does not store collections in S3 or a managed vector database. Local disk is used for simplicity and cost control. Acceptance Criteria A reviewer can upload the full demo corpus and ask: What is FR-006? The answer should mention the retrieval-only endpoint and cite this product requirements document. A reviewer can ask whether authentication is included. The answer should state that authentication is not included in the current release. A reviewer can ask what success target is defined for fact-seeking questions. The answer should report the 85 percent target. A reviewer can ask whether scanned PDFs are supported. The answer should say OCR is not included and text must be extractable.

For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time. For numeric spreadsheet questions, the system should report exact values from the workbook and avoid rounding unless asked. The model may cite a filename even when the retrieved snippet does not support the statement. Spreadsheet rows may be missed if a sheet is too large and relevant rows are split away from headers. The answer model may over-answer when the user asks about information that is absent from the corpus. Very broad questions may retrieve generic overview chunks instead of the most specific operational details. Recommended Improvements After Baseline Add a small evals folder with question, expected answer, expected source, and answer_should_exist fields. Add a retrieval-only test that calls /retrieve and checks whether expected sources appear in the top five results. Add reranking if the vector retriever returns plausible but weak context. Add hybrid keyword and vector search if exact IDs, codes, or named clauses are often missed. Add stronger PDF parsing or OCR only if the target documents require it.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. sources.text: Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.

sources.text: For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time. For numeric spreadsheet questions, the system should report exact values from the workbook and avoid rounding unless asked. Failure Modes to Watch The retriever may return a semantically similar but wrong document when multiple files discuss the same feature. The model may cite a filename even when the retrieved snippet does not support the statement. Spreadsheet rows may be missed if a sheet is too large and relevant rows are split away from headers. The answer model may over-answer when the user asks about information that is absent from the corpus. Very broad questions may retrieve generic overview chunks instead of the most specific operational details. Recommended Improvements After Baseline Add a small evals folder with question, expected answer, expected source, and answer_should_exist fields. Add a retrieval-only test that calls /retrieve and checks whether expected sources appear in the top five results. Add reranking if the vector retriever returns plausible but weak context. Add hybrid keyword and vector search if exact IDs, codes, or named clauses are often missed. Add stronger PDF parsing or OCR only if the target documents require it.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

sources.text: Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health. If the backend direct health check works but the Nginx-routed health check returns 404, the Nginx site is probably not linked, the default site is still enabled, or Nginx was not reloaded. The intended service names are insight-api and insight-ui.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The secondary persona is a recruiter or technical reviewer evaluating whether the project demonstrates practical RAG engineering, deployment awareness, and clear explanation of tradeoffs. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. Personas The primary persona is an early-career analyst who has several PDFs, Word files, and spreadsheets and wants quick answers without reading every page manually. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx INSIGHT.AI Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .insight_data for Windows development and /opt/insight-ai/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time. For numeric spreadsheet questions, the system should report exact values from the workbook and avoid rounding unless asked. Failure Modes to Watch The retriever may return a semantically similar but wrong document when multiple files discuss the same feature. The model may cite a filename even when the retrieved snippet does not support the statement. Spreadsheet rows may be missed if a sheet is too large and relevant rows are split away from headers. The answer model may over-answer when the user asks about information that is absent from the corpus. Very broad questions may retrieve generic overview chunks instead of the most specific operational details. Recommended Improvements After Baseline Add a small evals folder with question, expected answer, expected source, and answer_should_exist fields. Add a retrieval-only test that calls /retrieve and checks whether expected sources appear in the top five results. Add reranking if the vector retriever returns plausible but weak context. Add hybrid keyword and vector search if exact IDs, codes, or named clauses are often missed. Add stronger PDF parsing or OCR only if the target documents require it.

A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx INSIGHT.AI AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/insight-ai/data. The environment file should live at /opt/insight-ai/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/insight-ai/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/insight-ai/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/insight-ai/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/insight-ai/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart insight-api insight-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health. If the backend direct health check works but the Nginx-routed health check returns 404, the Nginx site is probably not linked, the default site is still enabled, or Nginx was not reloaded. The canonical backend port is 8000, but it should only bind to localhost. The canonical UI port is 8501, but it should only bind to localhost. The intended service names are insight-api and insight-ui.

Document filename: 01_product_requirements.docx INSIGHT.AI Product Requirements Document Version 2.4 - Demo Corpus Executive Summary INSIGHT.AI is a document assistant for retrieval augmented generation over uploaded business documents. The product goal is to let a user upload project material, create a searchable collection, and ask grounded questions with visible source evidence. The demo release is designed for small to medium public documents. It is not intended for confidential legal, medical, financial, or customer records because the final language model answer may be generated by an external model provider. The product success target for the demo is to answer at least 85 percent of fact-seeking test questions correctly when the answer exists in the uploaded documents, while refusing unsupported questions when the answer is absent. The tertiary persona is a project manager who wants comparison summaries across release notes, budgets, risk logs, and deployment documents. Functional Requirements FR-001: The system shall accept PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads through a browser user interface. FR-002: The system shall create named searchable collections. A collection name must be sanitized before it is used as a storage path. FR-003: The system shall preserve uploaded source files under local storage so a collection can be reloaded after service restart. FR-004: The system shall use local embeddings to avoid sending full documents to the answer generation model. FR-005: The system shall return source snippets with each answer so the user can inspect which chunks were retrieved. FR-006: The system shall expose a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. FR-007: The system shall warn users that AWS hybrid mode sends retrieved excerpts to Groq for final answer generation. FR-008: The system shall keep API keys, uploaded documents, and generated indexes out of Git. Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx INSIGHT.AI RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/insight-ai/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.
